title: A quantile bound showed high positive-count ranks in selected USGS sequence-specific aftershock forecasts
abstract: We test the count of aftershocks conditional on at least one event, using a fixed published USGS archive from 2019-2026. A quantile-only lower bound avoids reconstruction of the full count distribution. For shallow mainshocks, complete magnitude thresholds and occurrence probability at least 0.2, issued sequence-specific Reasenberg-Jones forecasts supplied 1,032 units from 11 mainshocks, with 629 positive outcomes. The event-weighted mean rank lower bound was 0.673, against a calibration reference of 0.5. A mainshock-bootstrap 95% interval was 0.586-0.749. Each mainshock omission left a bound of 0.656-0.702. Without one-year windows the interval included 0.5. The pooled event-weighted result gave no such evidence. This exploratory result concerns selected issued model labels, not all aftershock forecasts. Overlapping windows, few mainshocks, outcome-dependent version counts, analyst selection and revised catalogs limit inference. We give a proof, offline input tables, source attribution, code, independent arithmetic checks and all aggregate results. The test does not identify a cause or validate a forecast repair.

display.caption: Lower bounds on positive-count ranks by issued model and weighting. Bars show exploratory 95% mainshock-bootstrap intervals. Only a bound above 0.5 gives evidence in the high-count direction.

citations.reason: We reuse verified licensed tables and test positive counts, a target distinct from pooled occurrence calibration.
